passages.title: Community Charity Fair
passages.text: Last Saturday, our school held [1: a charity fair] to collect money for families in need. At the entrance, we met [2: energetic volunteer] who explained the activities. She showed us [3: the small map] of the stalls; it was the only map displayed beside the gate. Our class had prepared [4: a hundreds of paper flowers] for sale. Near the library, [5: an university student] offered advice on running a business. During the afternoon, I helped [6: a elderly visitor] find a quiet seat. Later, the visitor thanked me and joined [7: the music workshop] that she had booked earlier that morning. My friend Leo needed [8: rest] after carrying heavy boxes for two hours. We sat under a tree and watched students perform. Before leaving, the teacher reminded us that [9: teamwork] matters more than winning prizes. We finally counted the donations and discovered that our class had raised more money than expected. The head teacher said our efforts had made [10: a positive difference] to the community.

passages.title: A Rainy Evening in the Neighbourhood
passages.text: At seven o'clock yesterday evening, heavy rain caused flooding in several streets. A reporter arrived at [11: scene] near our estate to interview residents. She first spoke to [12: the shopkeeper] from a nearby shop that had not been mentioned before. The shopkeeper said water had entered his store within minutes. Soon [13: an emergency worker] arrived and guided people to safety. One resident was taken to [14: the hospital] for treatment after falling on the wet pavement; the report is describing the patient receiving hospital care, not a visit to a building. Another resident felt cold but did not suffer from [15: a hypothermia]. According to [16: local weather officer], the amount of rain recorded during the storm was unusually high. The officer showed the reporter a chart and explained why [17: rainfall] from this storm had exceeded the usual level. By midnight, workers had cleared the drains. [18: The workers] remained until the streets were safe. The following morning, the council promised [19: an detailed inspection] of older pipes and warned that [20: several delay] were possible if the rain returned.

passages.title: The Lost Notebook
passages.text: On Monday, a student named Marcus discovered [21: the blue notebook] under an empty seat on a bus. Nobody had mentioned the notebook before, and it had no owner's name. When Marcus opened it, he found [22: an unusual drawing] on the first page. The drawing showed a mountain and a river. He also saw [23: a old photograph] between two pages. Marcus gave the notebook to the driver and asked whether it belonged to anyone. The driver placed it beside [24: the ticket machine], which was the only machine near his seat. At the next stop, [25: elderly man] entered and asked about a missing notebook. He explained that he had lost it while travelling to visit his daughter. Marcus recognised the photograph and handed him [26: notebook] he had found. The man smiled with relief and thanked Marcus for [27: a honesty]. He said that the notebook contained [28: several important memory] from his childhood. He was so tired after searching that he needed [29: a rest]. Marcus was pleased to have done [30: a good deed] before reaching school.

passages.title: Planning a Science Exhibition
passages.text: Our class is preparing for a science exhibition next month. The organisers have chosen [31: a main hall] for the displays, but they have not announced which hall yet. Maya wants to demonstrate [32: an useful device] that saves electricity. Ben plans to build a model of a bridge and has ordered [33: the wooden blocks] from an online shop; these blocks have not been identified before. Our teacher says everyone should receive [34: advice] before starting an experiment. We will also invite [35: a MTR engineer] to explain public transport technology. The engineer's name has not been decided, so the guest is still unknown. Each group must prepare a poster, and [36: the poster] produced by our group must include our test results. Our team has already bought one thermometer. During the exhibition, visitors will be able to see [37: thermometer] on our table. The school is offering [38: scholarship] to the student with the strongest research proposal; only one award is available and it has not yet been assigned. I hope we can make [39: a meaningful contribution]. After the event, we will upload our findings to [40: a school website], which everyone in our school already uses.

passages.title: A Letter About a New Routine
passages.text: Dear Emma, I hope you are well. Since moving to this district, I have changed several habits. On weekdays, I travel to school by [41: the bus], but I walk home when the weather is fine. Last month, I joined [42: a reading club] at the community centre. It was my first visit, and I did not know any of the members. The club leader gave me [43: an interesting book] about the history of Hong Kong. Two days later, I returned [44: book] to her because she had asked to see it again. I also spend time at [45: the university] during open lectures; I mean the local institution's campus, and both of us know which university I mean. My cousin has just graduated from [46: the university] and is now looking for work; here I mean completing university education, not leaving a particular building. Last week, I felt unwell and stayed in [47: the bed] all afternoon. Fortunately, I made [48: steady recovery] and went back to class. I have learnt that [49: patience] is important when habits change. Please write soon and tell me whether you have developed [50: an new hobby]. Best wishes, Oliver.

steps: 先看句子在說甚麼：學校第一次介紹一場慈善活動。
把事情的關係排清楚：一場未指定是哪一場的活動；先看數量、是否第一次出現，以及讀者能否辨認。
找出最重要的提示：句中最重要的資料是「學校第一次介紹一場慈善活動」。
決定要用哪種寫法：在這個意思下，應寫「a charity fair」，因此填「TICK」。
把答案一步一步寫出來：fair 是單數可數名詞；charity /ch/ 開頭→a。
比較最容易混淆的另一個寫法：the charity fair 需要大家已知道是哪一場。
放回完整句子，再做最後檢查：Last Saturday, our school held a charity fair to collect money for families in need.  最後問自己：名詞在這裡是單數、複數還是不可數？是否已經知道是哪個？

比較最容易混淆的另一個寫法：the volunteer 表示之前已知道是哪位。
放回完整句子，再做最後檢查：At the entrance, we met an energetic volunteer who explained the activities.  最後問自己：名詞在這裡是單數、複數還是不可數？是否已經知道是哪個？

比較最容易混淆的另一個寫法：a small map 只表示不特定的一張。
放回完整句子，再做最後檢查：She showed us the small map of the stalls; it was the only map displayed beside the gate.  最後問自己：名詞在這裡是單數、複數還是不可數？是否已經知道是哪個？
先看句子在說甚麼：hundreds of 後面說很多紙花。

把答案一步一步寫出來：a hundreds→刪去 a→hundreds。
比較最容易混淆的另一個寫法：a hundred of flowers 是另一個數量結構，並非 a hundreds。
放回完整句子，再做最後檢查：Our class had prepared hundreds of paper flowers for sale.  最後問自己：名詞在這裡是單數、複數還是不可數？是否已經知道是哪個？

先看句子在說甚麼：搬箱後要休息一次。

決定要用哪種寫法：在這個意思下，應寫「a rest」，因此填「a」。
把答案一步一步寫出來：rest 在這個片語作一次休息→a。
比較最容易混淆的另一個寫法：rest 作一般抽象概念時可不用冠詞；need a rest 是常用說法。
放回完整句子，再做最後檢查：My friend Leo needed a rest after carrying heavy boxes for two hours.  最後問自己：名詞在這裡是單數、複數還是不可數？是否已經知道是哪個？
先看句子在說甚麼：團隊合作是一般概念。

決定要用哪種寫法：在這個意思下，應寫「teamwork」，因此填「TICK」。
把答案一步一步寫出來：泛指 teamwork→不用冠詞。
比較最容易混淆的另一個寫法：the teamwork 可指某次特定合作，但這裡泛指合作精神。
放回完整句子，再做最後檢查：Before leaving, the teacher reminded us that teamwork matters more than winning prizes.  最後問自己：名詞在這裡是單數、複數還是不可數？是否已經知道是哪個？
先看句子在說甚麼：努力帶來一項正面影響。

比較最容易混淆的另一個寫法：the difference 需要指定哪項影響。
放回完整句子，再做最後檢查：The head teacher said our efforts had made a positive difference to the community.  最後問自己：名詞在這裡是單數、複數還是不可數？是否已經知道是哪個？

比較最容易混淆的另一個寫法：a scene 可泛指一個場景，但本句是事故現場。
放回完整句子，再做最後檢查：A reporter arrived at the scene near our estate to interview residents.  最後問自己：名詞在這裡是單數、複數還是不可數？是否已經知道是哪個？

先看句子在說甚麼：句子強調傷者送院接受治療。

先看句子在說甚麼：from this storm 明確指出本次降雨。

決定要用哪種寫法：在這個意思下，應寫「the rainfall」，因此填「the」。
把答案一步一步寫出來：特定雨量→the。
比較最容易混淆的另一個寫法：rainfall 作一般概念時可不用冠詞。
放回完整句子，再做最後檢查：The officer showed the reporter a chart and explained why the rainfall from this storm had exceeded the usual level.  最後問自己：名詞在這裡是單數、複數還是不可數？是否已經知道是哪個？

決定要用哪種寫法：在這個意思下，應寫「The workers」，因此填「TICK」。
把答案一步一步寫出來：再次提及→the。
比較最容易混淆的另一個寫法：Workers remained 可能泛指一群未指定工人。
放回完整句子，再做最後檢查：The workers remained until the streets were safe.  最後問自己：名詞在這裡是單數、複數還是不可數？是否已經知道是哪個？
先看句子在說甚麼：市政局承諾安排一次詳細檢查。
把事情的關係排清楚：一次新提出的檢查；先看數量、是否第一次出現，以及讀者能否辨認。
找出最重要的提示：句中最重要的資料是「市政局承諾安排一次詳細檢查」。
決定要用哪種寫法：在這個意思下，應寫「a detailed inspection」，因此填「a」。
把答案一步一步寫出來：detailed /d/ 開頭→a。
比較最容易混淆的另一個寫法：an detailed 的 d 是輔音聲。
放回完整句子，再做最後檢查：The following morning, the council promised a detailed inspection of older pipes and warned that several delay were possible if the rain returned.  最後問自己：名詞在這裡是單數、複數還是不可數？是否已經知道是哪個？
先看句子在說甚麼：several 表示多次延誤。
把事情的關係排清楚：多於一件，所以名詞用複數；先看數量、是否第一次出現，以及讀者能否辨認。
找出最重要的提示：句中最重要的資料是「several 表示多次延誤」。
決定要用哪種寫法：在這個意思下，應寫「several delays」，因此填「PLURAL: delays」。
把答案一步一步寫出來：delay→delays，several 後接複數。
